subject: science
passage: Diamond and graphite are both made of nothing but carbon atoms, yet the two materials could hardly be more ______. Diamond, in which each atom is locked tightly to four neighbors, is the hardest natural substance known. Graphite, whose atoms form flat sheets that slide easily over one another, is so soft that it leaves marks on paper and is used in pencils.
stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical and precise word or phrase?

explanation.why: "Yet" signals a contrast with the fact that both materials are made of the same atoms. The rest of the text shows diamond as extremely hard and graphite as very soft. The blank must stress how unlike each other they are, so "different" fits.
explanation.A: Incorrect. "Yet" sets up a contrast with their shared makeup, and the text goes on to show that one is very hard and the other very soft. "Comparable" says the opposite.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The text compares hardness and softness, not worth, and it never says graphite is valuable.
explanation.C: Correct. Though made of the same atoms, diamond is the hardest natural substance and graphite is soft enough to use in pencils, so they could hardly be more different.
explanation.D: Incorrect. The text says nothing about how common either material is.
